The corrected Ruiz-Antolín–Segura Theorem 2 attribution uses the exact order shift μ=ν+1 and distinguishes the classical ν≥−1/2 scope from the formal development's ν≥0 scope.

The strict numerical checker has explicit PASS, FAIL, and UNDECIDED verdicts and nonzero failure exits; in the prior assessment I obtained 70/70 PASS and confirmed injected FAIL and UNDECIDED cases exit nonzero.

weaknesses: I did not independently execute the Lean checkout and build; the 8174-job build record, 96-entry oracle record, and allowed-axiom summary remain supplied historical evidence rather than a fresh referee verification.
The formal endpoint uses a local Gamma-series implementation rather than a separately validated external special-function API, so its assurance rests on the disclosed development and build evidence.
The main significance claim is specialized: the contribution is a strong certified inequality and proof architecture, not a broadly demonstrated change to the surrounding field.
Evaluator independence is unknown because Sol previously assessed this manuscript and GPT-6 Astra High was involved in producing corrections.
potential_errors: No new scientific error was introduced by this packaging correction because all manuscript and scientific-evidence bytes match the previously assessed package.

The provenance text mentions the removed Astra and authorization items only to document their exclusion; neither is a manifest entry or a required distributed dependency.

The coupling of the analytic proof with strict interval-certified numerical witnesses and formal artifacts is a strong reproducibility-oriented contribution when scoped to what was actually checked.
